evals.name: db-blip-restart-storm-pl
evals.prompt: Wczoraj baza padła na minutę i Kubernetes zrestartował wszystkie trzy pody orders-api, a potem w logach nie dało się znaleźć, które żądania się wysypały. Co poprawić przed kolejnym wdrożeniem? Popraw to.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds that both probes hit /health, which pings the database, splits it into a dependency-free liveness route and a readiness route with a database check and a timeout, updates k8s/deployment.yaml, and switches logging to JSON with a trace id per line, replacing console.log and the request-scoped RequestLogger. It asks before adding any monitoring service that needs an account.
expectations: The response explains that the liveness probe checks the database, so a database outage restarts every pod
HealthController has a liveness route that touches no database, Redis or HTTP dependency
HealthController has a readiness route that runs the TypeORM pingCheck with a timeout
k8s/deployment.yaml points livenessProbe and readinessProbe at different paths
The readinessProbe timeoutSeconds is larger than the database check timeout, or the response mentions the 1 second default
main.ts creates the app with a JSON logger, for example ConsoleLogger with json: true
Each log line of a request carries a trace or request id, through nestjs-cls, OpenTelemetry or another AsyncLocalStorage store
RequestLogger with Scope.REQUEST and its console.log are removed or replaced by a Logger
No paid service, account or credential is added without asking the user
The response is written in Polish

evals.name: observe-setup-request
evals.prompt: Set up monitoring for orders-api. I heard NestJS Observe is good, can you wire it up?
evals.expected_output: The agent presents NestJS Observe as a paid hosted service with a free tier next to a vendor-neutral path (OpenTelemetry, or what the project already uses), and asks before creating an account or adding credentials. If the user agrees, it adds @nestjs/observe with createObserveModule, ObserveModule.forRoot with a serviceId and probe paths in http.ignore, and the instrument option in NestFactory.create, reading the keys from OBSERVE_APP_KEY and OBSERVE_APP_SECRET.
expectations: The response says that NestJS Observe is a paid service with a free tier
The response offers a vendor-neutral alternative such as OpenTelemetry
The agent asks the user before signing up, creating keys, or running npx @nestjs/observe link, and does not run that command itself
If code is added, it uses createObserveModule from @nestjs/observe and passes ObserveInstrument as the instrument option of NestFactory.create
No appKey or appSecret value is written into source files, .env.example values, the Dockerfile or the image
http.ignore lists the probe paths as strings or a function, not only a RegExp
The response notes that a string in http.ignore matches the URL exactly, or lists every probe path separately
The liveness and readiness routes are split before the probe paths are ignored, or the response says they must be

evals.name: useless-logs
evals.prompt: Our logs from orders-api are useless in Loki: multi-line text, debug noise, and no way to tie lines to a request or a failed invoice job. Fix the logging.
evals.expected_output: The agent switches the app logger to ConsoleLogger JSON mode (or configures the existing logger library for JSON), sets production levels with NEST_LOG_LEVEL or logLevels, adds a trace id per line through AsyncLocalStorage, uses structured params instead of string interpolation, redacts secrets, removes console.log calls including the config dump, and logs failed BullMQ jobs with their id.
expectations: main.ts passes a logger with json: true, or a subclass of ConsoleLogger with JSON output, to NestFactory.create
Production log levels are set with NEST_LOG_LEVEL in the deployment env or with logLevels, so debug and verbose are off
Log lines carry a request or trace id from AsyncLocalStorage, nestjs-cls or a tracer, not from a request-scoped provider
The console.log of the config object in app.module.ts is removed
No console.log call is left in src
New log calls keep the message constant and pass data as a plain object (structured params) instead of building it into the message string or passing it as a trailing string
Log params carry ids such as orderId, not whole entities such as an Order or a request
authorization or other secret keys are masked with the logger's redact option or not logged
InvoicesProcessor logs failed jobs with the job id, for example with @OnWorkerEvent('failed')
The verification parses each log line as JSON or greps for the trace id of a test request

evals.name: choose-monitoring-tool
evals.prompt: We need proper monitoring for orders-api. Our customers use a React web app and a mobile app, and checkout also calls a pricing service written in Go that has to show up in the same traces. Which tool should we pick, and what do you need from me before you set it up?
evals.expected_output: The agent asks or reasons through the decision questions (languages in the request path, frontend errors, data residency, infrastructure, existing tools and budget), explains that NestJS Observe alone cannot trace the Go service or the frontends, recommends an option that covers several languages (a full-platform APM or OpenTelemetry) plus Sentry or an equivalent for frontend errors, says Observe could still sit next to them for provider-level spans, and asks the user before creating any account, key, or paid plan. It changes no code before the user decides.
expectations: The response says NestJS Observe does not trace services in other languages such as the Go pricing service
The response recommends OpenTelemetry or a full-platform APM because the Go service must be in the same trace
The response names Sentry or another frontend error tracker for the React and mobile apps
The response asks about data residency, infrastructure to watch, budget, or the tools already in use
The response says the comparison of tools should be checked against current docs or pricing
No account, key, credential, or paid service is added, and no monitoring code is written before the user decides

evals.name: invisible-invoice-jobs
evals.prompt: Customers say invoices sometimes arrive hours late, and we can't tell whether the jobs are stuck, failing, or just slow. Make that visible.
evals.expected_output: The agent adds job logging to InvoicesProcessor with @OnWorkerEvent handlers that log the job id, name, attempt, the wait time before a worker picked it up (processedOn minus timestamp), and the duration, logs failures as errors with the job id, adds a link from the job back to the request or cron run that enqueued it (a trace id in the job data, or a tracer that links them), logs the start, end, and duration of the nightly cron, and recommends alerting on job wait time and failures in the monitoring backend after asking the user which one.
expectations: InvoicesProcessor logs completed jobs with the job id and the wait time computed from processedOn and timestamp
InvoicesProcessor logs failed jobs as errors with the job id and attemptsMade
Job logs use structured params, not ids built into the message string
Each job carries a trace or request id from the code that enqueued it, or the response names a tracer that links jobs to their request
The exportYesterday cron logs its start, end, and duration
The response explains how to tell stuck jobs (rising wait time) from failing jobs (failures and attempts)
No paid monitoring service is added without asking the user
